chunks: Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man found a dinar in his house. So he said: "Does someone other than him enter his house?" I said: "Yes, many." He said: "This is luqaṭah (lost property)."
I said: And a man found a dinar in his صندوق (box). He said: "Does anyone other than him put his hand into his box or place something in it?" I said: "No." He said: "Then it belongs to him."

key_terms.بَيْتِهِ: his house; a place that may be accessed by others
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a gold coin; the item found in the case discussed
key_terms.صُنْدُوقِهِ: his box or chest; a private container under his control
key_terms.فَهُوَ لَهُ: then it belongs to him; a ruling of ownership in this context
key_terms.لُقَطَةٌ: lost property that is subject to the rulings of found property

ai.seo_question: If someone finds money in his house or private box, is it treated as lost property or does it belong to him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about found money based on whether others have access to the place where it was found. If the place is commonly entered by others, the money is treated as luqaṭah (lost property); if it is found in a private box that no one else accesses, it is considered the finder’s own property.
